title: Shell.run launches a process off the main actor with three pipes, a working directory and an environment, and returns status plus both streams
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:36-56 - the @concurrent run(_:_:in:environment:input:timeout:outputLimit:) signature and its setup: executableURL, arguments, currentDirectoryURL only when a directory is given, environment defaulting to LoginEnvironment.current, stdout and stderr Pipes, a stdin Pipe only when input is non-nil, and standardInput set to FileHandle.nullDevice when there is no input

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:4-12 struct ShellResult - status: Int32, stdout: Data, stderr: Data, with succeeded == (status == 0), output and errorOutput decoding UTF-8, and trimmedOutput trimming whitespace and newlines
preconditions: An executable URL is known.
expected_result: The process runs off the main actor. With no directory argument the child inherits the app's own working directory rather than being given one. With no environment argument it gets LoginEnvironment.current. With no input, stdin is the null device, so a child that reads stdin sees EOF immediately rather than blocking. The result carries the raw exit status and both streams as Data; text accessors decode UTF-8 lossily via String(decoding:as:).
failure_cases: process.run() throws (missing or non-executable file): the error is rethrown to the caller through the continuation and no result is produced.
windows_path: CreateProcess-equivalent with three pipes and NUL as stdin when there is no input. Platform boundary: Windows has no direct equivalent of inheriting the parent's cwd selectively, and the child must be given an explicit environment block.
verification_method: contract fixture over a known child

title: Output is collected through readability handlers into tail-bounded buffers, trimmed only once a buffer holds twice the limit

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:261-284 OutputCollector.reader and append - empty data clears the handler and closes the stream; otherwise the chunk is appended under a lock, and when a limit exists and the buffer exceeds limit * 2 the buffer becomes its last `limit` bytes

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:278-280 - the comment: keeps the tail within the limit, trimming by whole chunks once the buffer holds twice the limit, so a stream that never ends costs O(limit) memory and amortized O(1) per byte

The head of a long stream is discarded, not the tail.

windows_path: Same two-times-limit hysteresis; do not trim on every append, and do not trim to exactly the limit at the end.
verification_method: unit test feeding chunks past the threshold and asserting the retained byte range

title: A command that outlives its timeout is terminated; the default timeout is 120 seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:42 - timeout: TimeInterval = 120 is the default parameter
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:81-85 - after a successful run() a deadline Task sleeps for the timeout and, unless it is cancelled, calls terminate(process)
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:63-68 and :103 - the deadline is cancelled in the defer and again after the status arrives
preconditions: A command is running.
expected_result: The process is terminated (PR-TERM-085) and the call returns with whatever exit status the termination produced, which is non-zero, so ShellResult.succeeded is false. The deadline task is cancelled as soon as the process exits normally, and again on the way out, so a finished command never gets killed late.

failure_cases: The caller sees a failed result rather than a thrown timeout error; the distinction between a timeout and an ordinary failure is not reported.
cancellation: The deadline itself is cancelled on normal completion.
windows_path: Same default of 120 seconds and the same silent degradation to a failed result. Platform boundary: the termination mechanism (PR-TERM-085).
verification_method: contract fixture with a sleeping child and a short timeout

title: Termination is a two-step ladder: terminate now, then kill the process group one second later if it is still running
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:110-118 terminate(_:) - returns unless the process is running; calls process.terminate(); then on a global .utility queue one second later, if it is still running, calls kill with -pid when getpgid(pid) == pid and with pid otherwise, sending SIGKILL
porting/critiques/triage_summary.json:92 - notes that neither call site uses setsid, so whether the group dies depends on the child
preconditions: A process is running and must stop.
action: terminate is called by the timeout or by cancellation.
expected_result: SIGTERM first. Exactly one second later, if the process is still alive, SIGKILL is sent to the whole process group when the process is its own group leader, and to the single process otherwise. The one-second gap and the group-leader test are both load-bearing: a child that is not a group leader has only itself killed, so its own children survive.
side_effects: Signals are delivered; grandchildren may or may not die depending on the group test.
failure_cases: A child that is not a group leader can leave grandchildren running. This is upstream behaviour and is not repaired.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY. Windows has no signals and no process groups in this sense. The closest faithful shape is a graceful stop request followed one second later by a forced termination, with the tree-versus-single distinction resolved by a Job Object. Whether the port kills the tree or only the process must be an explicit engineering decision that records the difference from the source, not a silent choice.
verification_method: contract fixture with a child that spawns a grandchild

title: The login environment is captured once by running the user's shell as an interactive login shell around a marked env dump, with an 8-second budget
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:363-381 read() - marker "__DROPPY_CODE_ENVIRONMENT__"; script is printf of the marker, then /usr/bin/env -0, then printf of the marker; the shell is run with ["-l", "-i", "-c", script] with the fallback environment and timeout 8; the region strictly between the first and last marker occurrence is split on NUL; each entry is split at its first '='

preconditions: The app is starting.
expected_result: The user's shell runs its login and interactive profiles and prints its whole environment NUL-separated between two copies of the marker. Only the region between the first and the last marker is parsed, and only when the first ends before the last begins, so profile output before or after the dump is ignored. Entries with an empty key or a key in the excluded set are dropped. Entries with no '=' are skipped. Values may contain '=' because only the first one splits. The whole read is abandoned after 8 seconds, leaving the fallback environment.
side_effects: The user's shell profile files are executed, which can have arbitrary effects.
persistence: None on disk; the result is cached in memory for the run.
failure_cases: The shell fails, times out, or prints no markers: the fallback environment is used with only the PATH augmentation applied.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY. Windows processes inherit the user environment directly, so the login-shell read has no purpose. The replacement is a read of the process environment plus the user and machine Environment registry keys. This is an explicit decision, not a translation. Tracked as UNK-0005.
verification_method: contract fixture with a scripted shell emitting markers, plus the no-marker and timeout cases

title: The environment load is single-flight: concurrent callers await the same task
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:328-330 - the comment: the one read of the login shell; launch starts it, and anything that resolves a CLI before it lands waits on the same task, so a codex under nvm is never reported missing

preconditions: Several call sites may need the environment before the capture finishes.
expected_result: Exactly one capture runs. Every caller awaits the same task and returns when it completes. A reader that does not await, using `current` directly, gets the process fallback environment until the capture lands, which is why anything resolving a CLI awaits load() first.

failure_cases: A caller that reads current without awaiting during the window sees the fallback PATH and can report a CLI as missing. The single-flight await exists precisely to avoid this.

windows_path: Same single-flight discipline around whatever the Windows capture becomes.

title: start() installs both read handlers and the termination handler before launching, and tears them down and finishes the stream if the launch throws
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:49-82 start() - the stdout handler consumes data or, on empty data, clears itself and calls finishOutput; the stderr handler appends or, on empty data or a dead self, clears itself; the termination handler calls didExit; then try process.run(), and on a throw both handlers are cleared, the continuation is finished and the error is rethrown
preconditions: A StdioProcess has been constructed.
action: start() is called and the executable cannot be launched.
expected_result: Both readability handlers and the termination handler are installed first. If run() throws, both handlers are removed, the message stream is finished so every consumer's loop ends cleanly, and the error propagates to the caller. A successful launch leaves the handlers in place.
side_effects: A child process is launched on the success path.
failure_cases: Launch failure yields a finished, empty message stream plus a thrown error; consumers must not hang.
windows_path: Same ordering and the same cleanup on a failed launch.
verification_method: contract fixture with a missing executable

title: send() serializes a message on a private serial queue and frames it as a line or behind a Content-Length header
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:84-98 send(_:) - on the writeQueue, the message's data is taken; for .lines the payload is the body plus a single 0x0A; for .contentLength it is "Content-Length: \(body.count)\r\n\r\n" as UTF-8 followed by the body; the write uses try? and its error is ignored
DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:20 - the queue is labelled "droppycode.stdio.write"
preconditions: The child is running.
expected_result: Writes are serialized on one queue, so messages cannot interleave. Line framing appends exactly one LF and no CR. Content-Length framing emits the header name with that exact capitalization, a colon, a space, the byte count of the body, CR LF CR LF, then the body, with no other headers. Write errors are swallowed.
side_effects: Bytes are written to the child.
failure_cases: The child has exited: the write fails silently and the message is lost with no error surfaced.
windows_path: Same framing bytes exactly, and the same single serial write queue. The header must not gain a Content-Type line.
verification_method: unit test comparing the emitted bytes for both framings

title: write() sends raw bytes unframed and closeInput() closes the child's stdin, both on the same write queue

preconditions: The child is running.
action: A caller pipes a prompt and then closes stdin.
expected_result: The raw bytes are written with no framing added. Because both operations use the same serial queue, a close issued after a write always happens after that write completes. Both swallow their errors.
side_effects: Bytes written; the child sees end of input after the close.
failure_cases: Writing after the close fails silently.
windows_path: Same ordering guarantee through one serial writer.
verification_method: contract fixture piping a prompt to a one-shot child

title: StdioProcess.terminate closes stdin first, then terminates, then kills after three seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:114-123 terminate() - the stdin handle is closed on the writeQueue; the method returns early unless the process is running; otherwise process.terminate() and, three seconds later on a global queue, kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) when it is still running
preconditions: A child is to be stopped.
expected_result: stdin is always closed, even when the process has already exited, which is what lets a child that is waiting on input finish on its own. Then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL three seconds later if needed. Note the kill targets the single pid, NOT the process group, which differs from Shell.terminate (PR-TERM-085) and from its one-second gap. Both asymmetries are in the source and are kept.
side_effects: Signals are delivered to the child only; grandchildren are not targeted.
failure_cases: A grandchild that inherited stdout keeps it open past the child's exit; PR-TERM-114 handles that separately.
windows_path: Same order and the same three-second gap, and the same single-process (not tree) scope, so the two ladders stay distinguishable. Platform boundary: graceful stop and forced termination in place of the two signals.
verification_method: contract fixture with a child that ignores the graceful stop

title: Each delivered frame has trailing carriage returns and spaces stripped, and empty or unparseable frames are dropped silently
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:138-148 consume and deliver - frames come from the framer under the lock; deliver removes trailing bytes while they are 0x0D or 0x20, then requires a non-empty line and a successful JSONValue.parse before yielding to the stream
preconditions: The child is emitting output.
expected_result: Trailing CR and space bytes are stripped in a loop, so CRLF line endings and trailing padding both work. A frame that is empty after stripping is dropped. A frame that is not valid JSON is dropped with no diagnostic: a CLI that prints a banner line to stdout simply has that line ignored. Leading whitespace is NOT stripped.

title: The message stream is finished when stdout closes, and again one second after the child exits, because a grandchild can hold stdout open
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:150-153 finishOutput - flushes the framer's remainder through deliver, then finishes the continuation

DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:173-178 - the comment: a grandchild can inherit stdout and keep it open after the provider exits; one second after the exit, the stdout readabilityHandler is cleared and finishOutput is called
DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:57-59 - an empty read also clears the handler and calls finishOutput
preconditions: The child has exited or closed stdout.
expected_result: Any partial frame left in the framer is delivered first (and dropped if it does not parse), then the stream finishes, which is what ends the consumer's read loop. Because AsyncStream.Continuation.finish is idempotent, calling it from both paths is safe. The one-second delay bounds how long a consumer waits on a stream held open by a grandchild.

windows_path: Same two termination paths and the same one-second bound. Platform boundary: handle inheritance on Windows must be restricted so a grandchild does not hold the pipe, or the same bound applied.
verification_method: contract fixture with a child that leaves a grandchild holding stdout
